intro.author: 'The elder' (v. 1), traditionally the apostle John; some scholars think it was another church leader known as John the Elder
intro.written: Probably about AD 85–95, around the time of 1 John
intro.audience: 'The elect lady and her children' (v. 1), most likely a local church and its members, since the letter closes with greetings from 'thy elect sister' (v. 13); some think an individual woman is meant
intro.setting: Traveling teachers depended on believers' hospitality as they moved between churches. Some of them were 'deceivers' who denied that Jesus Christ had come in the flesh (v. 7), the same error 1 John confronts.
intro.purpose: The elder encourages the church to keep loving one another and walking in the truth, and warns them not to welcome or support false teachers.
intro.bigIdea: Walk in love and truth together, and do not give deceivers a welcome.

outline.title: Love, truth and a warning about deceivers

commentary.t: THE SECOND AND THIRD EPISTLES GENERAL OF JOHN
